explanation.Summary: This 12-second, 250 Hz single-lead screening detected 14 beats. Mean heart rate was 72.009 bpm, with detected rates from 71.77 to 72.115 bpm. Quality was marked "ok"; this is not a medical diagnosis. Educational screening tool, not a medical device.
explanation.What the numbers mean: Mean RR was 833.231 ms. RR SDNN 1.922 ms describes spread, RMSSD 3.266 ms describes successive-interval change, pNN50 0% is the proportion differing by more than 50 ms, and RR CV was 0.0023. These include all detected beats and are not adjudicated NN HRV. Heuristic SNR was 30.35 dB.
explanation.Possible findings: The supplied finding is suggestive of regular RR timing within the screened rate range, with a 0.75 confidence badge. This badge is heuristic, not a validated disease probability. Regular timing does not establish sinus rhythm or exclude a condition. RR irregularity alone cannot establish AFib.
explanation.Limitations: This is a short, single-lead rate-and-RR screen. No PR, QT, ST, QRS-width, axis, or lead-morphology assessment is available. No ECG image was inspected, so image calibration cannot be assessed. Filtering may distort the first and last 0.5 seconds. Ectopy or detection errors can affect variability.
explanation.When to see a doctor: Have a clinician review the result, especially if there are symptoms or concerns. Seek urgent care for chest pain, fainting, or severe shortness of breath.
